title: Deliberately awkward: long headline, one-word last lines, long everything
note: Written to stress the layout: a 27-word headline, body copy whose last line would be one word, very long checklist items, a long stat value and a long button label. Shows what the layout and the checker do when the copy is wrong for the format.

slides.headline: Everything nobody tells you about hiring your first employee, and why waiting another six months will probably cost you far more than the salary ever would
slides.sub: A long read in seven slides.

slides.headline: Why hiring slowly feels safe
slides.body: Waiting feels responsible because the cost of a bad hire is vivid, while the cost of doing everything yourself is invisible and quietly compounding.

slides.headline: Write the job around the problem you have this month, not the company you hope to build in three years
slides.body: Describe the work, the first thirty days and what good looks like. Skip the wish list. Candidates can tell.

slides.headline: Before you post the role
items: You can describe the first ninety days of work in two plain sentences without using the word synergy
You know what you can pay, and you have said it out loud to someone
Someone other than you has read the job post and understood it

slides.label: in work you did yourself instead of growing the business
slides.note: An invented number to test a long value. Do not quote it.

slides.before: I will hire when revenue is steady and I have a proper onboarding process written down and approved.
slides.after: You wait for a calm month that never comes, and the process only ever gets written after someone joins and asks for it.

slides.headline: Hire the first one before you feel ready
